I have farmed these 15 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years, and I know every plot. Ten mu are in the wheat-maize double crop, and five mu go to cotton. Last year my wheat made about 550 kg per mu, the maize about 600 kg per mu, and the cotton gave me about 260 kg of seed cotton per mu. This year I want to push the wheat to 580 kg and the maize to 650 kg, but I have to watch my spending because only my wife and I are working the land full-time, though my son sends some money back from his factory job.

I visited the input dealer in town last month, and I also listened to the county TV extension program. They showed soil tests saying potassium is getting low around here after so many years of wheat-maize without enough K replacement. So I am changing my mix. For the 10 mu of winter wheat, I will sow an improved variety, about 15 kg of seed per mu. I will apply 16 kg of nitrogen per mu total: I put down compound fertilizer at sowing that gives about 8 kg N, then topdress with urea at the jointing stage in late March for another 8 kg N. I am keeping phosphorus at 7 kg P2O5 per mu because my soil still has enough from years of compound use, but I am raising potassium to 7 kg K2O per mu to keep the wheat from lodging. I will irrigate four times with my well—wintering water, jointing, heading, and grain filling. For crop protection, I will spray once with herbicide before winter, once with insecticide for aphids in spring, and once with fungicide for powdery mildew, so three pesticide trips total.

For the summer maize on the same 10 mu, there is no time to plough after the wheat harvest, so I will use no-tillage direct seeding with a hybrid variety, one package per mu. I will apply 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu at sowing, then side-dress another 5 kg N as urea when the plants are at the 8-leaf stage. I will irrigate twice, at jointing and filling, and spray herbicide once plus insecticide twice for corn borers—three pesticide applications in total.

For the 5 mu of cotton, I will rotary till in mid-April and plant a hybrid Bt cotton, about 1.5 kg of seed per mu. Cotton is a heavy feeder on potassium, so I will apply 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 9 kg potassium per mu, using compound fertilizer as a base and urea at flowering. I will irrigate three times—seedling establishment, flowering, and boll filling. Cotton pests never rest, so I will spray 10 times through the season for bollworm, aphids, and spider mites. If the autumn weather holds, I expect 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.
